exposure: opioid poisoning in the year prior to pregnancy
opioid poisoning in the year following pregnancy
outcome: neonatal conditions associated with in utero hypoxia
cohort: Pregnant women in Western Australia identified from linked state midwifery, hospital, and emergency department data who experienced opioid poisoning between 2003 and 2018, along with their neonates.
finding: Opioid poisoning during pregnancy is uncommon, less likely to be intentional and involve multiple substances, and is associated with an increased risk of conditions associated with in utero hypoxia in neonates.
